name: Construction cost escalation index (US, selling-price basis)
seriesName: Turner Building Cost Index (US nonresidential building selling-price index), annual average; 2026 = Q1-Q3 2026 average (YTD)

2026.method: Mid = Construction Analytics 2026 nonres 4.4% (e14), matching RLB YoY 4.45% (e11). Low = T&T 4.25% (e13). High = Q3 2026 quarterly momentum annualized (RLB +1.28%/qtr = 5.2%).

2027.method: Mid = median of the published US/North America forecasts: JLL NA mid 3.7% (e12), T&T 4.0% (e13), Construction Analytics 4.0% (e14) -> 4.0%. Low = JLL NA low 3.2%. High = current momentum (Turner Q3 2026 +1.48%/qtr = 6.1% annualized; RLB 5.2%), tempered. DoD 2.0% (e10) is budget guidance and is excluded from the midpoint.

2028.method: Mid = Construction Analytics 2028 4.0% (e14). Low/high = JLL 3-6% baseline band (e12). T&T Las Vegas 3.0% (e16) supports the low end.

2029.method: No published US point forecast found. Mid 4.0% = long-run anchors: Turner 2010-2025 CAGR 4.2% ((1485/799)^(1/15)-1, e1/e3) and Construction Analytics since-2011 average excluding 2021-22 = 3.9% (e15). Range = JLL 3-6% baseline (e12).

method: Primary series: Turner Building Cost Index, annual averages. It is a public, nationwide selling-price index covering labor rates and productivity, material prices and market competition (e4), i.e. what owners pay. 2010-2012 come from Turner's Q4 2022 release (e3); 2013-2025 from the Q3 2026 release (e1); the two releases agree on every overlapping year. 2026 = average of Q1-Q3 2026 (1530, 1552, 1575; e2) = 1552.3. This is a year-to-date value: Q4 2026 is not yet published, and Turner labels each quarter a 'forecast'. If Q4 follows the recent ~1.4%/qtr pace, the full-year average would be about 1564 (+0.7%). No year is interpolated. Escalation A->B = series[B]/series[A] (e.g. 2019->2026 = 1552.3/1156 = 1.343). Cross-checks (alternateSeries): BLS PPI final-demand construction (selling price, nonresidential buildings) 2019->2025 = 1.407 vs Turner 1.285. The PPI shows a larger 2022-23 jump and a flatter 2024-25. DoD SPI (blend of RLB, Turner and the BLS office PPI) 2010->2025 = 1.93 vs Turner 1.86. Input-cost PPIs are kept as alternates for residential and materials-heavy types. They exclude labor and margin, so they are not used as the primary series. forecast = annual escalation rates for years after the base-year mid-point (2026 rate covers the rest of 2026). 2027-2028 are midpoints of published forecasts; 2029-2030 are derived from long-run averages (see forecastRange). Note: 2026 Q3 momentum (Turner +1.48%/qtr, RLB +1.28%/qtr) runs above the 4.0% mid; tariffs on metals and energy are the main upside risk (RLB: input costs +8.9% YoY).

source.title: A Guide to Construction Cost Indexes (PPI explanation)

evidence.quote: Each month, BLS gets contractors' estimaties of what they would charge to construct buildings with those specifications. Thus, the indexes cover both materials costs and contractors' estimated overhead and profits.
evidence.scopeNotes: Final demand construction (WPUFD43) = weighted average of five new nonresidential building PPIs (warehouse, school, office, industrial, health care); a selling-price index. ('estimaties' is the source's spelling.)
